content.text: Auscultate:
Bruits: bell
abd aorta     -   renal arteries     -    iliac arteries      -    femoral arteries
rule of 2:     -    renal arteries: 2in above umbilicus, 2in lat      -    iliac arteries: 2in below umbilicus, 2in lat
Bowel Sounds: diaphragm,  5-10s @each location
Pitch                                                -    Loudness
Frequency: Hypoactive: < 5 /min, Normoactive: 5-34 /min, Hyperactive: ±35 /min
Borborygmi: norm -active digestion -> mvt of gas or fluid in GI tract -> rumbling, growling, gurgling
Causes:    -        digestion          -    diarrhea          -    hunger: loud stomach
med conditions: IBS, celiac disease, lactose intolerance
Prevent: eat slow, avoid trigger foods, tx dx
Percussion:
***percuss & palpate tender quadrant LAST***
Tympanic                           -    Dullness: fluid, gas, viscera or masses
LLQ:      -    constipation      -    solid organ       -   mass/tumor     -    full bladder
Liver:     -    liver span or liver scratch test
Percuss, start @below umbilicus RMCL: tympanic -> dull -mark
percuss, start @nipple RMCL -> resonant -> dulls -mark    -> Measure
Norm: 6-12 cm RMCL, 4-6cm in midsternal line    -  false (+) -enlrg:  -  Rt pleural effusion -  consolidation
Spleen
castells sign: percuss 9 - 10 ICS in Lt A. axillary line    ->     pt deep breath & percuss again
Norm: note ⍉chg             *Abnorm: note chg -tympany -> dull (beginning or after inspiration)
Traube’s sign: percuss Lt lower A. chest wall -6th ICS   ->   cont to A axillary line -down costal margin
Norm: tympany throughout         *Abnorm: dull -> splenomegaly
False (+): fluid or solids in stomach or colon
Kidney: 1 hand flat on CVA -> strike w ulnar of opposite fist          *Causes:   -     Pyelonephritis   -    kidney infection
Norm: ⍉tender                  *Abnorm:  tender
Bladder: Above pubic symphysis    -check for height & fullness         *bladder vol = + 400 - 600 mL = dull percussion
Palpation
Light: 1 hand over the other                *< 1cm depth in all 4 quad -> TENDER LAST
Deep: 2 hands: all 4 quadrants -> TENDER LAST
Feel for:   -   Masses     -   shape      -  consistency     -  Tenderness     -  Guarding      -  Rigidity     -  pulsations
Ticklish: palpate over pt hand -> ONLY SHOW TENDERNESS         -   Distract pt when trying to reprod pain
Guarding: voluntary vs involuntary: Involuntarily guarding -> Peritonitis
Have pt relax abd musc     -  have pt breathe w jaw open    -   palpate after exhale or distract pt
Liver:
direct deep palpation w inspiration: Palpate lowerer than expected to ⍉miss lower liver edge
hooks method to feel liver edge (press in w fingers up & toward costal margin -pt deep inhale
Norm to ⍉palpate, if feel: norm =smooth, non-tender, mod firm
too firm: hepatomegaly, cirrhosis, mets, CA, effusion, airtrapping
Spleen: 2 hands: place 1 under costal margin, 1 under flank -pt take deep breath
Best palpated in RLDP -Rt side w legs flexed -> gravity swings spleen down
⍉palpable in norm
Kidney: 2 hands: 1 hand on A. abd side, 1 underneath torso to lift kidney towards other hand
⍉palpable in norm
Aorta: above umbilicus in epigastrium area             *AAA Sx: enlrg aorta +3cm              -    2.5cm =norm
Non-tender,  regular rhythmic pulse
Bladder: smooth, round if distended   -check tenderness in suprapubic area              * ⍉smooth: mass, tumor
⍉palpable in norm
Special Tests
Hemorrhage
Cullen’s Sign: periumbilical bruising -ecchymosis  ->
intraperitoneal bleeding
Causes:           -    trauma             -    fallopian tube rupture -ectopic preg       -    abscess
Grey Turner’s Sign: ecchymosis on flank -unilat or B/L  ->
retroperitoneal bleeding
Causes:           -    trauma             -    non-trauma -ex. hemorrhagic pancreatitis
Acites: Causes:   -  cirrhosis     -  portal HTN           Caution:    -  ⍉detect sm amount of fluid   -  false (+): obese pt
Tests:
fluid wave: pt ulnar surface on abd midline
My hands on B/L pt flank -> tap 1 side & feel distinct tap w other hand (repeat B/L)
↓false (+) from attributing  adipose tissue to fluid
shifting dullness: fluid shifts to flanks b/c gravity
-> percuss across abd & listen for chg tympany in center -> dullness lat
Peritonitis
Hx:  how was the drive here/pot holes/bumps -pain (Merkle’s Sign)
Rebound Tender: press in then quickly release
+ =pain on withdrawal              -    Pain away from palpation location =poss peritonitis
Cutaneous Hyperesthesia:  Stim cutaneous abd n.: gently stroke skin w nail or pen
↑sensitivity or pain = peritoneal inflam -gen peritonitis or zone
Markel’s Test (Jar Test) -whole body percussion: bump table or bottom of pt feet -> abd pain -> peritonitis
Peds: “Simon says” -> pt jump on 1 foot, or stand on tippy toes & drop to floor
Appendix:
MC S/Sx,
US & CT
Acute appendicitis Sx:  -  periumbilical pain localized to RLQ    -   pain worse w mvt    -  pain b4 emesis
-  fever
Stool caught in appendix path -> bacterial infect          ** MC-E.coli & Bacteroides Fragilis
Pain from: fluid, gas, peritoneal & organ stretch: visceral -> somatic pain w progression
RLQ peritonitis                 -    periumbilical tender                        -
early involuntary guarding
McBurney’s Sign: tender, 1/3 distance: ASIS  -umbilicus OR 2/3 distance: umbilicus - ASIS
rebound tender:
pain due to stretch & bounce of peritoneum
Rovsing’s Sign: referred pain in RLQ during LLQ rebound tender -> appendicitis
Psoas Sign:
ask pt raise Rt leg at hip against resistance: contract psoas muscle
Mvt of psoas musc under inflamed peritoneum -> pain (appendicitis)
Passively induce irritation: pt lay on Lt side -> extend Rt thigh P. ->stretch psoas musc
Obturators Sign:  pt flex Rt hip & knee 90’ -> internally rotate hip -contract obturator musc -> irritation
Pain = local peritoneal irritation -appendix or PID
Considerations: pt have hip pain -> false (+)     * r/o hip pain: B/L test or palpate Rt hip for pain
Gallbladder: Murphey’s Sign: press  RUQ -> pt deep breath -> inspiratory arrest b/c pain  -> cholecystitis
Norm: norm, full inhale                     *Abnorm: halt inspiration due to pain
Spleen: Kehr’s Sign: referred pain to  Lt shoulder
-irritated diaphragm phrenic n.
-   Causes:   -  splenic rupture    -  splenic abscess   -  air under diaphragm  -  perforation intestine or stomach
Hernia: can pull peritoneum w hernia
Hernia Emergency:       -  ↑pain        -    new N/V       -     non-reducible (strangulated)
Assess Hernias:    -  Pt tuck chin to chest or valsalva       -    inspect for bulges, masses, surgical scars
auscultate over hernia for bowel sounds
-    palpate for soft, firm, reducible
Inguinal Hernia: AMAB >AFAB   -hole for spermatic cord -> bowel contents go through
Ventral Hernia: peritoneal lined-sac protrudes through abd wall defect
Diastasis recti or epigastric hernia:  separate rectus abdominis musc <-
weak or disrupt of linea alba
Common in 3rd tri of preg
Umbilical Hernias: fascial defect peri-umbilicus <- poss weakness since birth
MC in infants, pos
s spont close by 2yrs
*“Outie belly button”
Surgery if:   -   recurrent     -   non-reducible       -   N/V     -    Pain
Incisional Hernia: protrude through surgical wound healing site ->
MCC =wound dehiscence-sudden healing fail
stool softeners & narcotics post-surgery -prevent constipation -straining   *8-12wks -> ⍉ lift +5lbs
Abnormalities
Lrg Belly (6F’s):    -    Flatus: sm or lrg bowel obstruct            -    Fat                                          -    Fluid: ascites
-      Feces: constipation, palpable mass     -    Fetus: child bearing age     -     Fatal growth: tumors, CA
Pregnancy: qualify for free care in MI
Anatomy:
abdominal muscles: stretch            -    Compressed: stomach, gallbladder, liver, colon
bladder: ↓capacity
-    appendix: lat displacement
Considerations:
gestational age:      -   1st: 0-13 Wks     -   2nd: 14-27 Wks    -    3rd: 28-40 Wks
b-HCG levels: rise during 1st tri
↓levels in 1st tri: fetal demise -> measure serum b-HCG over couple days
pre-natal care: are they getting it?
is it problem w mom, baby or both?
vaginal bleeding?
Physical Exam: careful & thorough
Abd pain = ALWAYS DO PELVIC EXAM
ACUTE ABD DDX: in 1st tri = ectopic preg
DRE
Indication:  -  rectal pain or bleeding     -  constipation or fecal impaction   -  abd pain
-  prostate assessment  -  neuro status or back injury: assess rectal tone
Incontinence or no sensation = MC-spinal issue
-  sympathetic innervation (L1-L3)     -  parasympathetic innervation (S2-S4)
stool guaiac test: screening tool -> detect hidden blood in stool
stool sample -> guaiac card -> apply developer (+ = blue w/in 30s -2min)
Developer on back of stool sample card
False (+):      -     diet: pepto bismuth      -    vaginal bleeding       -     local bleeding: hemorrhoids
Pelvic Exam
Indication:    -    pelvic pain       -    abd pain        -    vaginal d/c        -    vaginal bleeding      -   r/o some DDx
Capture ovary : sm, ⍉ ridges, ⍉ tender
Speculum intra-vag-cervix -> look at tissue, blood, pus, walls
